name: Battle of Salamis

phases.title: The Persians block the southern exit
phases.text: The Allied fleet lay off Salamis, the Athenians on the left and the Spartans probably on the right. The Persian fleet was sent out to block the exit from the straits, and about 400 troops stood on Psyttaleia.

phases.title: The Persians pivot into the straits
phases.text: The Persians seem to have swung their fleet round off Cape Vavari, from a line across the exit to a line running north to south. The Phoenicians were on the right by Mount Aigaleo and the Ionians on the left.

phases.title: The Allies back their ships away
phases.text: As the Persians came on, cramped and disordered in the narrow water, the Allies seemed to back away as if in fear. Plutarch gave the reason as a better position and time to wait for the early morning wind.

phases.title: One ship rams and the whole line follows
phases.text: A single ship shot forward to ram the nearest Persian vessel, and the whole Greek line followed it towards the disordered Persian line. The Athenians and the Aeginetans each claimed the first ship as theirs.

phases.title: The Phoenicians are pushed back and the centre is split
phases.text: The first Persian line fouled the second and third behind it. The leaderless Phoenician squadrons were pushed back against the coast, many running aground, and in the centre a wedge of Greek ships split the Persian fleet in two.

phases.title: The Persian fleet retreats towards Phalerum
phases.text: The Persian fleet began to retreat towards Phalerum, and the Aeginetans ambushed it as it tried to leave the straits. The remaining ships limped back to the harbour and the shelter of the Persian army.

phases.title: Aristides destroys the garrison on Psyttaleia
phases.text: After the Persian fleet had limped back, the Athenian general Aristides took a detachment across to Psyttaleia to slaughter the garrison that Xerxes had left there.

note: The accounts do not say which shore lay on which side. Salamis is drawn on the west and the mainland with Mount Aigaleo on the east, which fits a Greek line running north to south with the Persian Phoenicians on the right next to Mount Aigaleo. The accounts give the fleets as lines, not as separate squadrons, so each block stands for a wing or the centre. One ancient account puts the Allied line north to south, another east to west, which is thought unlikely. The Allied right is probably the Spartans, though another account names the Megareans and Aeginetans. The Persians may have entered the straits at nightfall or only at dawn. Where the Aeginetans stood and where the detachment of Aristides set out from are not given, so they are placed by judgement. The Egyptian squadron sent round Salamis is left out, as only one account has it. The wedge that split the Persian centre is shown by the Allied centre pressing into it; the accounts do not place it more closely.
